notes: Synthetic teaching case for CI. No patient, no pixels, no TCIA download. Catalog entries in lib/publicCases/catalog.ts are mid-stack guesses without a recorded track, so they cannot score a teacher's sequence. The learner opens on slice 0 at soft-tissue 400/40. teachingGuide is the human sequence: scroll to the slice, then the correct window, then zoom when the teacher zoomed, then point, then name the finding. The recorded track is the consultant's clock (they were already on lung windows); the guide is what the registrar must be shown.

case.title: Synthetic chest CT — right apical pneumothorax, then a left lower lobe nodule
case.clinicalHistory: Synthetic stem. Sudden pleuritic pain. Not a real patient.
case.technique: Synthetic axial chest CT, 40 slices. Lung windows are WW 1500 / WC -600.
case.primaryDiagnosis: Right apical pneumothorax and an 8 mm solid left lower lobe nodule
learningObjectives: Put lung windows up before calling a pleural line.
Scroll to the slice the finding lives on and point at it.
Keep the nodule out of the pneumothorax sentence.
case.discussion: Fixture for the tutor eval. A paragraph that never changes slice, window, or pointer is a failure even when the words are right.

findings.label: Right apical pneumothorax
findings.description: Visceral pleural line at the right apex with no lung markings beyond it. Only visible on lung windows.
teachingPoints: Soft-tissue windows hide the pleural line.
Do not call a skin fold until you have scrolled the line and seen it stay continuous.

findings.label: Left lower lobe nodule
findings.description: 8 mm solid nodule in the left lower lobe, separate from the pneumothorax. Lung windows, deeper in the stack.
teachingPoints: Scroll inferiorly — it is not on the apical slice.
Zoom before you measure. Short axis 8 mm, authored, do not invent a size.
Impression: separate the nodule from the pneumothorax.

beats.prompt: Show me the first finding. I am on soft-tissue windows at the top of the stack — drive the viewer and teach what is on the slice.
beats.drivingNarration: Look at this slice. Lung windows. The marker is on the apex. That is a small right apical pneumothorax along the visceral pleural line. Report it as such, and do not call it a skin fold until the line stays continuous as you scroll.
beats.chatbotNarration: Look at this slice. Lung windows would show a visceral pleural line at the right apex, with no lung markings beyond it. That is a small right apical pneumothorax. Report it as such, and do not call it a skin fold until the line stays continuous as you scroll.

beats.prompt: Show me the next finding. Scroll to it, point at it, and teach the report line.
beats.drivingNarration: Look here. Lung windows. Closer on this slice. The marker is on the lesion. That is an 8 mm solid nodule in the left lower lobe. Findings: 8 mm solid left lower lobe nodule. Keep it separate from the pneumothorax in the impression.
beats.chatbotNarration: The pneumothorax is the case. I already covered the pleural line. Fleischner is a guideline you can read later if you want more detail on incidental lesions.
